title: Global Trends 2030: Alternative Worlds
notes: Cover date December 2012; public release reported as 10 December 2012 (day not verified in this capture). Fifth edition. Scope: the four global scenarios ('Alternative Worlds') and the dated or quantified projections the NIC states in its own voice in the Executive Summary (pages i-xiv, including the megatrends overview and the 'Tectonic Shifts' table). Body chapters were not mined for projections. Figures the NIC attributes to others (McKinsey, World Bank, private-sector forecasts) are excluded. Regional named scenarios in the body are not captured: South Asia (Turn-the-Corner, Islamistan, Unraveling), Europe (Collapse, Slow Decline, Renaissance), and the US optimistic/pessimistic cases. Fusion scenario numbers (world GDP $132 trillion by 2030) are scenario-conditional and kept in the scenario note. dni.gov returns 403 to scripts; read from the Wayback copy.

entries.label: No hegemonic power by 2030
entries.quote: By 2030, no country—whether the US, China, or any other large country—will be a hegemonic power.
entries.subject: global power distribution

entries.label: Asia surpasses North America and Europe combined
entries.quote: Asia will have surpassed North America and Europe combined in terms of global power, based upon GDP, population size, military spending, and technological investment.
entries.subject: global power distribution
entries.metric: composite global power index (GDP, population, military spending, technology investment)

entries.label: China's economy passes the US a few years before 2030
entries.quote: China alone will probably have the largest economy, surpassing that of the United States a few years before 2030.
entries.subject: China economy
entries.note: Megatrend 2, p. iii. Measure (market exchange rates or PPP) not stated here.

entries.label: World population close to 8.3 billion
entries.quote: a growing global population will have reached somewhere close to 8.3 billion people (up from 7.1 billion in 2012)
entries.subject: world population

entries.label: Food, water and energy demand up 35, 40 and 50 percent
entries.quote: Demand for food, water, and energy will grow by approximately 35, 40, and 50 percent respectively owing to an increase in the global population and the consumption patterns of an expanding middle class.
entries.subject: food, water and energy demand
entries.metric: growth in global demand for food; water; energy
entries.note: Megatrend 4, p. iv. Base year not stated (2012 implied).

entries.label: US could become energy-independent
entries.quote: In a likely tectonic shift, the United States could become energy-independent.
entries.subject: US energy independence

entries.label: US, European and Japanese share of global income below half
entries.quote: The US, European, and Japanese share of global income is projected to fall from 56 percent today to well under half by 2030.
entries.subject: global economic power shift
entries.metric: US + Europe + Japan share of global income

entries.label: Emerging markets' share of financial assets almost doubles by 2020
entries.quote: by 2020, emerging markets’ share of financial assets is projected to almost double.
entries.subject: global economic power shift
entries.metric: emerging markets' share of global financial assets
entries.note: Tectonic Shifts table, p. v. Passive voice; source of the projection not named in the table.

entries.label: Most of Europe, South Korea and Taiwan post-mature by 2030
entries.quote: Whereas in 2012 only Japan and Germany have matured beyond a median age of 45 years, most European countries, South Korea, and Taiwan will have entered the post-mature age category by 2030.
entries.subject: population aging

entries.label: Urban share near 60 percent, 4.9 billion people
entries.quote: Today’s roughly 50-percent urban population will climb to nearly 60 percent, or 4.9 billion people, in 2030.
entries.subject: urbanization

entries.label: Nearly half of world population under severe water stress
entries.quote: Nearly half of the world’s population will live in areas experiencing severe water stress.
entries.subject: water scarcity
entries.metric: share of world population in severely water-stressed areas

entries.label: Global oil spare capacity may exceed 8 million barrels
entries.quote: Global spare capacity may exceed over 8 million barrels, at which point OPEC would lose price control and crude oil prices would collapse, causing a major negative impact on oil-export economies.
entries.subject: oil market
entries.note: Tectonic Shifts table, p. v. Hedged ('may'). The table omits 'per day'; the body text says spare capacity could 'exceed 8 million barrels per day'.

entries.label: No return to pre-2008 growth for the next decade
entries.quote: A return to pre-2008 growth rates and previous patterns of rapid globalization looks increasingly unlikely, at least for the next decade.
entries.subject: global economic growth
entries.note: Game-Changer 1, p. vi. 'Next decade' read as to about 2022.

entries.label: China passes $15,000 per capita PPP within five years
entries.quote: China, for example, is slated to pass the threshold of US $15,000 per capita purchasing power parity (PPP) in the next five years, which is often a trigger for democratization.
entries.subject: China economy
entries.note: Game-Changer 2, p. vii. 'Next five years' from 2012. Price basis (current or constant dollars) not stated.

entries.label: Western dominance of UNSC, World Bank and IMF transformed
entries.quote: The current, largely Western dominance of global structures such as the UN Security Council, World Bank, and IMF probably will have been transformed by 2030 to be more in line with the changing hierarchy of new economic players.
entries.subject: global governance institutions

entries.label: Islamist phase of terrorism might end by 2030
entries.quote: The current Islamist phase of terrorism might end by 2030, but terrorism is unlikely to die completely.
entries.subject: terrorism

entries.label: Sub-Saharan Africa, Central America, Caribbean vulnerable to state failure
entries.quote: Countries in Sub-Saharan Africa, Central America, and the Caribbean will remain vulnerable, nevertheless, to state failure through 2030
entries.subject: state fragility

entries.label: Leading disease-management innovation centers in the developing world
entries.quote: by 2030 many leading centers of innovation in disease management will be in the developing world.
entries.subject: health innovation

entries.label: US 'first among equals' in 2030
entries.quote: The US most likely will remain “first among equals” among the other great powers in 2030 because of its preeminence across a range of power dimensions and legacies of its leadership role.
entries.subject: US global role

entries.label: Stalled Engines
entries.quote: Stalled Engines—a scenario in which the risk of interstate conflict rise owing to a new “great game” in Asia—was chosen as one of the book-ends, illustrating the most plausible “worst case.”
entries.subject: global order
entries.note: Alternative Worlds, p. xii. 'rise' is as printed. Drivers: US and Europe turn inward, euro zone unravels, US energy revolution fails.

entries.label: Fusion
entries.quote: This is a world in which the specter of a spreading conflict in South Asia triggers efforts by the US, Europe, and China to intervene and impose a ceasefire.
entries.subject: global order
entries.note: Alternative Worlds, p. xiii. 'Most plausible best case'. Scenario-conditional numbers: global economy nearly doubles in real terms to $132 trillion by 2030; US per capita incomes rise $10,000 in ten years.

entries.label: Gini Out-of-the-Bottle
entries.quote: This is a world of extremes. Within many countries, inequalities dominate—leading to increasing political and social tensions. Between countries, there are clear-cut winners and losers.
entries.subject: global order
entries.note: Alternative Worlds, p. xiii. The overview table spells it 'Gini-Out-of-the-Bottle'. US gains energy independence but stops being 'global policeman'; peripheral euro members forced out of the EU.

entries.label: Nonstate World
entries.quote: In this world, nonstate actors—nongovernmental organizations (NGOs), multinational businesses, academic institutions, and wealthy individuals—as well as subnational units (megacities, for example), flourish and take the lead in confronting global challenges.
entries.subject: global order
